module_title: Union & Its Territory and Citizenship - Reorganization and Citizenship Act
introduction: At this level, we study the historical evolution of Indian states (from linguistic demands to the States Reorganization Act) and delve deeper into the legal provisions of losing citizenship as per the Citizenship Act of 1955.

core_concepts.title: Dhar Commission & JVP Committee (1948)
core_concepts.description: Both committees were formed to look into the reorganization of states on a linguistic basis. Both formally REJECTED language as the primary basis for the reorganization of states.

core_concepts.title: Creation of Andhra State (1953)
core_concepts.description: Following the death of Potti Sriramulu after a 56-day hunger strike, the government was forced to create the first linguistic state: Andhra State (by separating Telugu-speaking areas from Madras State).

core_concepts.title: States Reorganization Commission (SRC - Fazl Ali Commission)
core_concepts.description: Appointed in 1953, it ACCEPTED language as the basis of reorganization but rejected the 'one language, one state' theory. This led to the States Reorganization Act of 1956, creating 14 states and 6 UTs.

core_concepts.title: Loss of Citizenship
core_concepts.description: The Citizenship Act, 1955, prescribes three ways to lose citizenship: 1) Renunciation (voluntary giving up), 2) Termination (automatically lost when acquiring another country's citizenship), 3) Deprivation (compulsory termination by the Central government for fraud/disloyalty).

core_concepts.title: Article 2 vs. Article 3
core_concepts.description: Article 2 relates to the admission or establishment of NEW states that are not already part of the Union of India (e.g., Sikkim). Article 3 relates to the formation of or changes in the EXISTING states of the Union.

important_entities.name: Potti Sriramulu
important_entities.significance: His fast-unto-death triggered massive protests, forcing the government to concede the demand for linguistic states, starting with Andhra.

important_entities.name: Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar, and H.N. Kunzru
important_entities.significance: They were the three members of the highly influential States Reorganization Commission of 1953.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Does altering a state require a Constitutional Amendment?
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: No. Article 4 clearly states that laws made under Article 2 and Article 3 to change state boundaries or names are NOT considered constitutional amendments under Article 368. They are passed by a simple majority.

A bill to alter state boundaries (under Article 3) can be introduced in the Parliament ONLY with the prior recommendation of the President. The President must also refer it to the concerned state legislature for its views, though those views are NOT binding.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya formed the JVP committee.

exam_strategy_tips: Chronology of State Formation is a hot topic. Remember the first linguistic state (Andhra, 1953) and later ones like Gujarat/Maharashtra (1960), Nagaland (1963), and Haryana (1966).
Identify the difference between 'Termination' (automatic upon getting foreign citizenship) and 'Deprivation' (forced by the government due to fraud).
